title: OmniVia Chat Runtime Contract v1 - Conversation graph identity
description: Closes CGAP-042-001 (Conversation and Message identity) and CGAP-042-002 (MessageDerivation). Normative wire shapes for Conversation, Message, MessagePart and MessageDerivation, exactly as REF-042 §7.1-§7.4 and ADR-022 §4.1-§4.3, §4.14-§4.15 define them. Every record is closed. Committed Message and MessagePart content, author, structural parent, content hash and creation sequence are immutable after commit (REF042-RULE-002, ADR022-INV-001, ADR022-INV-002).

Conversation.title: Conversation
Conversation.description: A Workspace-scoped container for related Chat Messages, branch paths, participants, shares, exports and view state (REF-042 §4.1, §7.1). Not itself a linear transcript.

title.description: Shared display metadata. Not part of Message lineage (REF-042 §7.1).

defaultBranchId.description: When present, identifies an existing accessible branch (REF-042 §7.1). Not organisational truth and does not invalidate other branches (ADR-022 §4.6).

graphRevision.description: Increments only for durable graph changes.

MessagePart.title: MessagePart
MessagePart.description: An ordered, typed unit of Message content (REF-042 §4.4, §7.3). Not a DOM fragment; never reconstructed from rendered HTML. The set of parts belonging to a committed Message is immutable. Unknown types decode to an inert, display-safe fallback and generated executable UI is prohibited.

index.description: Stable order position of this part within its Message.

type.description: Open, dot-namespaced part-type code, for example `text`, `markdown`, `citation`, `table`, `warning`, `app.output`, `workflow.status` (REF-042 §4.4). Open by design so a compatible minor release can add types; an unrecognised type decodes to an inert, display-safe fallback and is never executed.

payload.description: Type-specific closed payload envelope. The exact per-type payload shapes are owned by the Chat Part-type registry (out of scope for REF-042 and for this contract per REF-042 §2.2); this field is deliberately an opaque, schema-versioned object boundary rather than an invented catalogue.

provenance.description: Optional origin class for this part, aligned to DOC-004 §8.4 ProvenanceSourceKind by concept, not by shared schema.

Message.title: Message
Message.description: An immutable semantic Chat node authored by a user, assistant or another supported actor type (REF-042 §4.3, §7.2, ADR-022 §4.1). After commitment, canonical content, parentMessageId, author identity and creation sequence never change (ADR022-INV-001, ADR022-INV-002, REF042-RULE-002).

messageId.description: Stable and unique within the Workspace.

parentMessageId.description: Immutable structural parent. Absent means the conceptual Conversation Root (REF-042 §4.2, §4.5). At most one incoming lineage edge per Message (REF-042 §4.9).

authorId.description: Present when authorType names an identifiable principal.

parts.description: Ordered, typed Message Parts comprising this Message (REF-042 §4.3). Order is stable and the set is immutable once committed.

createdOnBranchId.description: Optional creation provenance only. Never canonical branch membership (REF042-RULE-007).

tombstonedAt.description: Present only when this Message has been tombstoned under a governed redaction procedure (REF-042 §25.2). A tombstone never implies the Message never existed (REF-042 §25.4).

MessageDerivation.title: MessageDerivation
MessageDerivation.description: A typed relation stating that one immutable Message was created from another immutable Message, without making the source a structural parent (REF-042 §4.10, §7.4, CGAP-042-002). Closes CGAP-042-002. Source and derived Messages always share Workspace and Conversation; amendment and regeneration source/derived pairs always share role and structural parent (REF042-INV-008, REF042-INV-009); derivation edges are acyclic and point from newer derived Messages to older source Messages.

metadata.description: Optional, non-authoritative derivation metadata. Never replaces lineage (REF-042 §7.4).
